producer_report.summary: ci.yml now restores and, on the default branch only, saves caches for gitleaks and the athena binary. Every job that runs the setup step restores them first. `setup.sh --ci` skips the gitleaks install and the athena build when the cached copy is present and matches, and prints that it skipped them. A new policy test fails when a job runs setup without the restore steps before it. CHANGELOG.md has an entry. I ran `cargo test -p xtask` (all tests pass); fmt and clippy were left to Athena. The speed-up on GitHub Actions is not measured here.

checks_run.note: all xtask unit and integration tests, incl. skip tests, policy, ci_shards

criteria_check.criterion: Grep of .github/workflows/ci.yml: in each of the fmt, clippy and test jobs, an actions/cache/restore step for gitleaks and one for the athena binary come before the step named 'Set up (pinned toolchain, gitleaks, athena)'. Each key uses hashFiles over the files that decide the install. Every `uses:` line is still pinned by a 40-character SHA.
criteria_check.evidence: ci.yml edited earlier; policy test every_job_restores_the_tool_caches_before_it_runs_the_setup_step and ci_shards workflow_actions_are_pinned pass in cargo test -p xtask.

criteria_check.criterion: ci.yml has matching actions/cache/save steps for those two caches in the same jobs. Each carries the existing condition: not a pull request, ref equal to the default branch, and no exact cache hit. Neither cache is saved from any other event.
criteria_check.evidence: Save steps added with the existing guard; ci_shards workflow_caches_* and policy tests pass.

criteria_check.criterion: The history, attribution and pr-head jobs that also run the setup step get the same restore step before it, or the diff states in a comment why they do not.
criteria_check.evidence: The policy test every_job_restores_the_tool_caches_before_it_runs_the_setup_step checks every job running setup and passes.

criteria_check.criterion: With a cached gitleaks and athena binary present and matching, `./setup.sh --ci` skips both installs and prints that it skipped them. Without them it installs as before. Run `cargo test -p xtask`, which must include a test that exercises the skip and no-skip decisions.
criteria_check.evidence: xtask/src/main.rs prints 'gitleaks ... already installed ...; skipped the install' and '--ci: skipped the athena build; the cached binary at ... matches the current sources'. Tests a_cached_athena_is_skipped_only_when_present_and_matching, a_cached_gitleaks_is_skipped_only_when_it_reports_the_pinned_version and the_inputs_digest_changes_with_a_source_and_ignores_other_files cover skip and no-skip; cargo test -p xtask ran: 50 unit tests plus all integration tests passed.

criteria_check.criterion: The new test in xtask/tests/policy.rs reads ci.yml and passes on the changed file. A test that feeds it a ci.yml variant with the restore step removed or placed after the setup step makes it fail. Run `cargo test -p xtask --test policy`.
criteria_check.evidence: cargo test -p xtask ran policy.rs: every_job_restores_... passes on real file; the_tool_cache_check_fails_when_a_restore_is_missing_or_after_setup passes; 14/14 passed.

criteria_check.criterion: `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` and `cargo test` all pass, including xtask/tests/ci_shards.rs and the existing policy tests.
criteria_check.evidence: left to Athena's checks; ci_shards.rs (20) and policy.rs (14) passed in my cargo test -p xtask run.

criteria_check.criterion: CHANGELOG.md has a new entry describing the gitleaks and athena binary caches and their keys, and stating that the speed-up is not measured here.
criteria_check.evidence: CHANGELOG.md modified with the entry (git status shows M).

mistakes: The previous report did not tie the skip criterion to its tests; fixed by running cargo test -p xtask and citing them.
learnings: The install and skip logic lives in xtask/src/main.rs; setup.sh just execs xtask setup, so it needs no change.
